name:	interfere-inc/landmines
description:	Oxlint rules that keep AI-written code honest: real implementations, real signals, no flake masking.
--
# landmines

Oxlint rules that keep AI-written code honest.

Coding agents are fast, and they optimise for green checks. Left alone, they
mock the thing under test, sleep until a race usually goes their way, retry
the flake, raise the timeout, and narrate the diff in comments. Every one of
those passes CI. None of them is true.

`landmines` makes the honest path the only one that lints. Each rule fails
with a message that tells the agent (or the human) what to do instead, so the
fix lands in the same loop that tripped it.

Built and used in production at [Interfere](https://interfere.com).

## Install

```sh
bun add -d oxlint @interfere/landmines
```

Extend the recommended configuration in `.oxlintrc.json`:

```json
{
  "extends": ["./node_modules/@interfere/landmines/configs/recommended.json"]
}
```

Or register only the plugins you want:

```json
{
  "jsPlugins": [
    { "name": "landmines-testing", "specifier": "@interfere/landmines/testing" }
  ],
  "rules": {
    "landmines-testing/no-test-doubles": "error"
  }
}
```

Requires Oxlint 1.81 or later and Node 22.18 or later.

## Rules

### `landmines-testing`

Tests that can't lie.

| Rule                 | What it stops                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no-test-doubles`    | Replacing dependency behaviour in tests: module mocks, `vi.fn(impl)`, stubbed globals, patched prototypes, hand-written bindings and fake responses. Use the real implementation and MSW for the network. Observation-only spies are allowed. |
| `strict-msw`         | Starting MSW without `onUnhandledRequest: "error"`, so unmocked requests silently reach the network.                                                                                                                                          |
| `no-fixed-sleep`     | Awaiting a fixed real-time delay in a test or hook. Await the operation or a signal it emits.                                                                                                                                                 |
| `no-unsignaled-poll` | `expect.poll` and `vi.waitFor` on request recorders and spy state, which race a deadline instead of awaiting an event.                                                                                                                        |
| `no-flake-masking`   | Test retries and raised timeouts. A test that passes on rerun is a flake to fix.                                                                                                                                                              |

`no-fixed-sleep`, `strict-msw` and `no-flake-masking` accept a per-file
allowlist with an exact count, so you can adopt them in an existing codebase
and ratchet down:

```json
{
  "landmines-testing/no-flake-masking": [
    "error",
    { "allow": { "src/legacy/slow.test.ts": 2 } }
  ]
}
```

The rule reports when a file has fewer violations than its allowance, so the
list only shrinks.

### `landmines-style`

| Rule          | What it stops                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `no-comments` | Prose comments. Allowed: functional directives (`oxlint-disable`, `@ts-expect-error`, `/* @__PURE__ */`, licence headers…), single-line `// WARNING:` comments for dangerous recurring footguns, and TSDoc on exported public API. Rationale belongs in the PR. |

Pass `publicApi` (regular expressions matched against the file path) to allow
TSDoc only in your published packages:

```json
{
  "landmines-style/no-comments": ["error", { "publicApi": ["/packages/sdk/"] }]
}
```

### `landmines-structure`

| Rule              | What it stops                                                                                                                         |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `colocated-tests` | Tests detached from the implementation they import. Tests live beside their subject or in its local `tests/` directory.               |
| `test-file-names` | `.spec.ts`, `.tests.ts`, `helpers.ts`, `mocks.ts` and friends. Use `.test.ts`, `.fixture.ts` and `.test-utils.ts`.                    |
| `package-exports` | Unrestricted source exports such as `"./*": "./src/*.ts"`. Declare explicit entrypoints or named public namespaces in `package.json`. |

### `landmines-types`

| Rule                       | What it stops                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `no-explicit-return-types` | Annotated return types on implementations. Let them be inferred; pin a contract with `satisfies` where it matters. |

## Pairs well with

- [anti-slop](https://github.com/dmmulroy/anti-slop) for type-level slop:
  chained assertions, unsafe dictionaries, `unknown` plumbing.

## Contributing

```sh
bun install
bun run lint && bun run typecheck && bun run test
```

Add a changeset with `bun changeset` for any user-facing change.

## License

MIT

# Lint scope

`oxlint.config.ts` replaces the old `.oxlintrc.json`. It extends `ultracite/oxlint/core` 8.1.1, the config the rat-stack reference uses, and loads the plugins #205 names: `surveybeat`, `no-comments`, `foldkit` (scoped to the Foldkit app), `anti-slop`, `anti-slop-effect`, `effect-tests`, `patterns`, and `xstate-effect` (from `@xstate/effect/oxlint`). 421 rules run at `error`; the ones that are not at `error` are listed below by name.

## Adopted surface

- `surveybeat/domain-boundary`, `surveybeat/privacy-query`, `surveybeat/no-literal-ui-text` stay, because they encode ADRs the reference does not have.
- `@foldkit/oxlint-plugin` recommended, mapped to `error` and `off` only; its `rules` are scoped to `apps/web/src/**/*.ts` and never to `apps/web/src/answer/**`, per ADR 0008.
- Vendored anti-slop: `tools/oxlint/anti-slop/` (18 generic rules and 5 Effect rules, MIT, `UPSTREAM.md` records `dmmulroy/anti-slop` at `c44ef22ca116d0ba62a3ff663a0bd13a3f3fa40b`).
- `effect-tests/no-manual-effect-runtime-in-tests` at `error`. The three `Effect.runSync` calls in `Themes.privacy.test.ts` were moved to `it.effect`, not suppressed.
- The five pattern rules at `error`: `no-module-level-mutable-state`, `no-shared-pending-cache`, `no-sleep-in-loop`, `shared-waiters`, `acquire-release-constructs-in-acquire-body`. `MainWorker`'s request-scoped `Effect.cached` was replaced with the plain `authSettings` Effect; the remaining `apps/web/src/messages/**` module state is exempted by scope (see below).
- Every adopted rule has a fixture: `tools/oxlint/fixtures/` holds a violating file per rule and `tools/oxlint/rules.test.ts` runs real oxlint over them, the same way `tools/oxlint-plugin-surveybeat/index.test.ts` does. `xstate-inline.ts` and `xstate-declared.ts` are the pair for `xstate-effect/no-inline-effect`: the first discards an Effect in an inline `enq` action and spawns inline Effect logic, the second declares both in `setupEffect` and passes only their names.

## Scope exceptions

Each is an `overrides` entry that names the rule and the files it cannot apply to.

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";
import { describe, expect, it } from "vitest";

const fixtures = fileURLToPath(new URL("fixtures", import.meta.url));

interface Diagnostic {
  readonly code: string;
}

const lint = (file: string): ReadonlyArray<Diagnostic> => {
  const result = spawnSync(
    "pnpm",
    ["exec", "oxlint", "--config", "oxlint.fixtures.json", "--format", "json", file],
    { cwd: fixtures, encoding: "utf8" },
  );
  const report: { diagnostics: ReadonlyArray<Diagnostic> } = JSON.parse(result.stdout);
  return report.diagnostics;
};

describe("the adopted rule set reports its own violations", () => {
  it.each([
    ["packages/slop/src/no-reflect.ts", "anti-slop(no-reflect-get)"],
    ["packages/slop/src/sleep-in-loop.ts", "patterns(no-sleep-in-loop)"],
    ["packages/slop/src/module-state.ts", "patterns(no-module-level-mutable-state)"],
    ["packages/slop/src/pending-cache.ts", "patterns(no-shared-pending-cache)"],
    ["packages/slop/src/shared-waiter.ts", "patterns(shared-waiters)"],
    ["packages/slop/src/eager-acquire.ts", "patterns(acquire-release-constructs-in-acquire-body)"],
    ["packages/slop/src/runtime.test.ts", "effect-tests(no-manual-effect-runtime-in-tests)"],
    ["packages/slop/src/xstate-inline.ts", "xstate-effect(no-inline-effect)"],
  ])("reports %s as %s", (file, code) => {
    const diagnostics = lint(file);
    expect(diagnostics.map((diagnostic) => diagnostic.code)).toContain(code);
  });

  it("reports both inline Effect forms in the xstate fixture", () => {
    const diagnostics = lint("packages/slop/src/xstate-inline.ts");
    expect(
      diagnostics.filter((diagnostic) => diagnostic.code === "xstate-effect(no-inline-effect)"),
    ).toHaveLength(2);
  });

  it("passes the xstate fixture that declares its actors", () => {
    expect(lint("packages/slop/src/xstate-declared.ts")).toHaveLength(0);
  });
});

diff --git a/.githooks/post-commit b/.githooks/post-commit
index ef233146..51a8a3d5 100755
--- a/.githooks/post-commit
+++ b/.githooks/post-commit
@@ -1,4 +1,17 @@
 #!/bin/sh
-set -eu
-root=$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)
-exec node "$root/scripts/fence/post-commit.mjs"
+# Entire CLI hooks
+# Post-commit hook: condense session data if commit has Entire-Checkpoint trailer
+if command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then entire hooks git post-commit 2>/dev/null || true; else :; fi
+# Chain: run pre-existing hook
+_entire_hook_dir="$(dirname "$0")"
+if [ -z "${ENTIRE_CHAINING_POST_COMMIT:-}" ]; then
+    ENTIRE_CHAINING_POST_COMMIT=1
+    export ENTIRE_CHAINING_POST_COMMIT
+    if [ -n "${PRE_COMMIT_RUNNING_LEGACY:-}" ] && grep -q '^# File generated by pre-commit: https://pre-commit.com' "$_entire_hook_dir/post-commit.pre-entire" 2>/dev/null; then
+        if [ -x "$_entire_hook_dir/post-commit.legacy.pre-entire" ]; then
+            "$_entire_hook_dir/post-commit.legacy.pre-entire" "$@"
+        fi
+    elif [ -x "$_entire_hook_dir/post-commit.pre-entire" ]; then
+        "$_entire_hook_dir/post-commit.pre-entire" "$@"
+    fi
+fi

content.text:
I've set up `@interfere/landmines` in this repo and committed it on `t3/setup-landmines-repo`. Nothing is pushed. Lint, typecheck, format, both ledgers, the 1218 unit tests and the fence gate (which includes the privacy tests) all pass.

**What's on:**
- **At `error`:** every `landmines-testing` rule (no mocking, no fixed sleeps, no polling without a signal, MSW must reject unmocked requests, no retries or raised timeouts) and every `landmines-structure` rule (tests sit next to their code, test file naming, explicit package exports).
- **One allowance:** `no-flake-masking` permits exactly 5 raised timeouts in `Organization.test.ts` and 1 in `Email.test.ts`. Those are the slow tests that deploy to local workerd. If a file drops below its count, the rule reports it, so the list can only shrink.
- **Off for now:** `landmines-types/no-explicit-return-types` had 748 findings. I added it to `restyleExceptionsOff` with that count, so it's part of the cleanup tracked in #216.
- **Not loaded:** `landmines-style/no-comments`. The repo's own `no-comments` rule already covers this, and the landmines version reports the `@effect-diagnostics … -- reason` directives and the JSDoc types the scripts need (575 findings).

**Code I changed instead of adding exceptions:**
- Two App test files replaced the browser's `navigator` with a stub, which `no-test-doubles` blocks. Now `initialModel` takes the browser languages as an argument, so tests pass `[]`. I updated the calls in `App.scene.test.ts`, `App.story.test.ts` and `overview.test.ts`. `overview.test.ts` had been picking up the host machine's real language until now.
- Six API tests failed `colocated-tests` because they imported a test harness from `auth/`. I moved `packages/cloudflare/src/auth/testing.ts` to `packages/cloudflare/src/testing.ts`, next to the handlers it wires.

Each adopted rule has a fixture that breaks it, checked in `tools/oxlint/rules.test.ts`. I also updated `docs/agents/lint-scope.md` and `AGENTS.md`.

**Decision for you:** version 0.1.0 was published on 2026-11-17, one day ago. When I installed it, pnpm added a `minimumReleaseAgeExclude` entry for it to `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, which bypasses the repo's waiting period for new packages. Keep it, or remove it and wait until the package is old enough.

Separately, Entire rewrote `.githooks/post-commit` and added five other hook files during this session. I left them out of the commit.

content.content: {"markdown":"[Skip to content](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets#blume-content) Opens in a new tab On this page - [ESLint Parity](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets#eslint-parity) - [TSDoc and Public API Documentation](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets#tsdoc-and-public-api-documentation) - [Anti-Slop Rules](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets#anti-slop-rules) - [Design System Rules with @shadcn/lint](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets#design-system-rules-with-shadcnlint) - [Agent Shortcut Rules with landmines](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets#agent-shortcut-rules-with-landmines) - [Authorization Proofs with gdp-ts](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets#authorization-proofs-with-gdp-ts) - [On ESLint](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets#on-eslint) # Optional Presets Opt-in Ultracite presets for ESLint parity, TSDoc, anti-slop rules, shadcn design systems, landmines and gdp-ts authorization proofs, and how to set each one up. Ultracite’s core and framework presets are on when you run `init`. The presets on this page are opt-in: each adds rules that suit some projects and not others, and most run through Oxlint’s JS plugin API, which is slower than Oxlint’s native rules. The JS plugin, TSDoc, anti-slop, `@shadcn/lint` and landmines presets are for Oxlint; the gdp-ts preset works with Oxlint and ESLint. ## [ESLint Parity](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets\#eslint-parity) The core preset — and the `react`, `next`, and `tanstack` framework presets — run entirely on Oxlint’s native, Rust-powered rules for maximum speed. If you want to close the remaining gap with the ESLint preset, Ultracite ships an opt-in `js-plugins` preset that runs [`eslint-plugin-github`](https://github.com/github/eslint-plugin-github), [`eslint-plugin-sonarjs`](https://github.com/SonarSource/eslint-plugin-sonarjs), and [`oxlint-plugin-react-doctor`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/oxlint-plugin-react-doctor) through Oxlint’s JS plugin support. TSDoc syntax and public API documentation checks are available as separate, explicitly selected plugins below; they are not added to the full preset, so existing users do not gain new dependencies when upgrading. This is **off by default** because it adds dependencies and runs a slower JavaScript lint pass instead of the native Rust one. You can enable it during setup: interactive `ultracite init` lets you choose individual JS plugins when you choose Oxlint, and non-interactive setup accepts package names via `--js-plugins`. npmpnpmyarnbunnubaube ``` npx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` pnpm dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` yarn dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` bunx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` nubx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` aube dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` React Doctor’s framework-specific rules are split into per-framework add-on presets so they only run where they apply — `nextjs-*` rules like `nextjs-no-img-element` fire on plain ``/`` JSX and would false-positive in non-Next.js apps. `init` wires these up automatically when you pick the matching framework together with `oxlint-plugin-react-doctor`: - `ultracite/oxlint/next/js-plugins` — React Doctor’s Next.js rules - `ultracite/oxlint/tanstack/js-plugins` — React Doctor’s TanStack Query/Router/Start rules If you’re adding the preset manually instead of through `init`, install the plugins yourself: npmpnpmyarnbunnubaube ``` npm install -D eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` pnpm add -D eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` yarn add -D eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` bun add -D eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` nub add -D eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` aube add -D eslint-plugin-github eslint-plugin-sonarjs oxlint-plugin-react-doctor ``` ``` import { defineConfig } from "oxlint"; import core from "ultracite/oxlint/core"; import jsPlugins, { jsPluginSettings } from "ultracite/oxlint/js-plugins"; export default defineConfig({ env: core.env, extends: [core, jsPlugins], ignorePatterns: core.ignorePatterns, jsPlugins: jsPlugins.jsPlugins, settings: jsPluginSettings, }); ``` In a Next.js or TanStack app, add the matching add-on preset as well: ``` import { defineConfig } from "oxlint"; import core from "ultracite/oxlint/core"; import next from "ultracite/oxlint/next"; import jsPlugins, { jsPluginSettings } from "ultracite/oxlint/js-plugins"; import nextJsPlugins from "ultracite/oxlint/next/js-plugins"; export default defineConfig({ env: core.env, extends: [core, next, jsPlugins, nextJsPlugins], ignorePatterns: core.ignorePatterns, jsPlugins: jsPlugins.jsPlugins, settings: jsPluginSettings, }); ``` ### [TSDoc and Public API Documentation](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets\#tsdoc-and-public-api-documentation) Two more JS plugins check the documentation in TypeScript files (`.ts`, `.tsx`, `.mts`, and `.cts`). They aren’t part of the full `js-plugins` preset, so they only run when you select them: - `eslint-plugin-tsdoc`, registered as `tsdoc`, validates [TSDoc](https://tsdoc.org/) syntax. - `eslint-plugin-jsdoc`, registered as `jsdoc-js` because Oxlint reserves `jsdoc` for its native plugin, requires a doc comment on every exported function, class, interface, type alias, and enum. It also covers the public methods and getters of exported classes, and exports that wrap a function, such as `export const Button = forwardRef(...)`. Selecting `eslint-plugin-jsdoc` also turns on Oxlint’s native `jsdoc/require-param` and `jsdoc/require-returns`, so every JSDoc comment on a function, exported or not, must describe its parameters and return value. Parameter and return types stay off, so TypeScript types aren’t repeated in comments. Selecting `eslint-plugin-tsdoc` adjusts core’s native `jsdoc/*` rules to fit TSDoc: tags such as `@remarks` and `@typeParam` are allowed, and generators don’t need `@yields`. With both plugins selected, a destructured parameter is documented by its own name (`@param props - ...`) rather than property by property. TSDoc has no `{Type}` syntax, so write the type on a `@throws` tag as a link: `@throws {@link RangeError} When the input is empty.` npmpnpmyarnbunnubaube ``` npx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` pnpm dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` yarn dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` bunx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` nubx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` aube dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` `--js-plugins` sets the whole selection, so list any plugins you already use, such as `eslint-plugin-github`. A config that extends the full `js-plugins` preset keeps its plugins. If you’re configuring Oxlint manually, install the plugins and select them: npmpnpmyarnbunnubaube ``` npm install -D eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` pnpm add -D eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` yarn add -D eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` bun add -D eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` nub add -D eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` aube add -D eslint-plugin-tsdoc eslint-plugin-jsdoc ``` ``` import { defineConfig } from "oxlint"; import core from "ultracite/oxlint/core"; import { selectJsPlugins } from "ultracite/oxlint/js-plugins"; const jsPlugins = selectJsPlugins(["tsdoc", "jsdoc-js"]); export default defineConfig({ env: core.env, extends: [core, jsPlugins], ignorePatterns: core.ignorePatterns, jsPlugins: jsPlugins.jsPlugins, }); ``` ## [Anti-Slop Rules](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets\#anti-slop-rules) Ultracite also ships an opt-in `anti-slop` preset built on [anti-slop](https://github.com/dmmulroy/anti-slop), Dillon Mulroy’s set of opinionated Oxlint rules that reject low-evidence, low-signal TypeScript and JavaScript patterns — unjustified type assertions, `unknown` leaking through function signatures, `Reflect`-based property access, module mocking, and similar escape hatches. Upstream is deliberately not published to npm (its distribution model is “copy the source into your repo”), so Ultracite vendors a self-contained bundled build of the plugin — there is nothing extra to install. Like `js-plugins`, this preset is **off by default** because it is strongly opinionated and runs through Oxlint’s slower JS-plugin pass. You can enable it during setup: it appears as `anti-slop` in the same JS-plugins prompt as the packages above, and non-interactive setup accepts it via `--js-plugins`: npmpnpmyarnbunnubaube ``` npx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins anti-slop ``` ``` pnpm dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins anti-slop ``` ``` yarn dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins anti-slop ``` ``` bunx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins anti-slop ``` ``` nubx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins anti-slop ``` ``` aube dlx ultracite init --linter oxlint --js-plugins anti-slop ``` Or add it to your config manually: ``` import { defineConfig } from "oxlint"; import antiSlop from "ultracite/oxlint/anti-slop"; import core from "ultracite/oxlint/core"; export default defineConfig({ env: core.env, extends: [core, antiSlop], ignorePatterns: core.ignorePatterns, }); ``` All eighteen rules are enabled at the `error` level, including `require-safety-comment-for-type-assertion` (every `as` assertion needs a `SAFETY:` comment stating the checked invariant), `no-unknown-returns` / `no-unknown-parameters` (parse values into named domain types at boundaries), `no-module-mocking` (inject dependencies instead of mocking modules), and `require-readable-spacing` (blank lines around top-level declarations, multiline bindings, control flow, returns, and blocks — a pattern AI-generated code tends to pack together; the fix only inserts whitespace, so `ultracite fix` restores the spacing without fighting the formatter). If a rule doesn’t fit your codebase — `no-module-mocking` is a common example in test-heavy projects — turn it off in your own config’s `rules` block. ## [Design System Rules with @shadcn/lint](https://www.ultracite.ai/docs/presets\#design-system-rules-with-shadcnlint) Ultracite also ships an opt-in `shadcn` preset built on [`@shadcn/lint`](https://github.com/shadcn-ui/lint), shadcn’s agent-first linter for Tailwind v4 design systems.
